Because these latter three keys share the departed key's tonic or differ from it by a single key-signature accidental, such changes are expected to retain $λ$ > 0.50 in a substantial proportion of cases. An event share G therefore assesses how often this expectation holds as tonal selectivity increases in 4-bar windows. The resulting high-G region identifies evidence-strength settings that may be appropriate for tonal-state inference. When $λ$ is extended to cross-scale compatibility, the Presto finale of Mozart's Piano Sonata K. 310 shows that, within this region, a 4-bar C-minor interpretation remains compatible with its 16-bar C-major context. The findings establish tonal continuity as a music-theoretical constraint on evidence strength and illustrate how local and prevailing-key interpretations can coexist when pitch evidence is integrated over nested spans.

title: Phase-resolved turbulence dynamics in cardiac-cycle-inspired pulsatile pipe flow
abstract: Direct numerical simulations examine the phase-dependent turbulence dynamics of pipe flow driven by cardiac-cycle-inspired waveforms. Four cases with and without a low-flow plateau span two Reynolds-number ranges. The response follows four stages of turbulent--turbulent reorganisation. Strong acceleration suppresses transverse fluctuations and vortical activity. During acceleration and early deceleration, streamwise-normal-stress production recovers ahead of pressure--strain redistribution and radial momentum transport, allowing energy to accumulate in elongated streaks. In early deceleration, near-wall high-speed streaks develop predominantly varicose disturbances associated with Q4 sweeps, whereas outer-buffer-layer low-speed streaks develop predominantly sinuous disturbances associated with Q2 ejections. The transition exhibits distinct radial sequences: Q2-based local onset occurs progressively later towards the wall, whereas Q4-based onset is nearly simultaneous across the viscous sublayer and buffer layer, with peaks occurring successively outwards. The two responses overlap between the drag minimum and recovery maximum as redistribution intensifies markedly and multiscale momentum transport recovers rapidly. Turbulence then decays and its scales readjust. Where present, the plateau prolongs this decay and weakens the turbulence inherited by the next acceleration stage. It further delays local instability and lengthens the onset-to-peak intervals of the shear contributions. An unsteady friction decomposition links these phase-dependent dynamics to the drag response, highlighting the role of delayed turbulent shear recovery in sustaining the low-drag interval.

title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
abstract: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gröbner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.

title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
abstract: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $Γ$ and $Λ$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $Γ$ and $Λ$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $Γ$ and $Λ$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $Γ$ to $Λ$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.

title: Scalable Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Exploration of Moire Patterns
abstract: Large materials design spaces often contain rare high-performing configurations that are difficult to identify through trial-and-error exploration or purely representative machine-learning (ML) sampling. In this work, we present FruBO, a flexible Bayesian Optimization framework for accelerating the discovery of optimal configurations in computationally demanding materials design problems. As a case study, we investigate multilayer Moiré patterns generated by the superposition of six rotated hexagonal lattices, where the objective is to identify the rotational conformation that maximizes pore-size uniformity, quantified using the Jain fairness index. The resulting benchmark contains 600,000 unique configurations and exhibits a highly skewed objective distribution, making the global optimum difficult to locate by random sampling. We compare random exploration, Gaussian Process-based Bayesian Optimization, and Bayesian Optimization using a lightweight CatBoost surrogate with committee-based uncertainty estimation. Random sampling identifies the global optimum only after 533,012 evaluations, requiring approximately 31 hours, while Gaussian Process-based BO becomes impractical due to GPU memory exhaustion after 290 acquired samples. In contrast, FruBO with CatBoost identifies the global optimum after 1,470 acquired samples and approximately 1.15 hours. These results demonstrate that scalable surrogate models can substantially improve the feasibility and efficiency of BO in large nanomaterials design spaces.

title: HIST3R: Decomposing and Rectifying State Updates with History for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction with recurrent states enables long-video scene understanding under bounded memory, but turns reconstruction into a state-evolution problem: each incoming frame updates a compact scene memory on which all subsequent predictions depend, so unreliable updates overwrite historical context and accumulate into long-horizon geometric drift. We analyze CUT3R-style recurrent updates through a direction--magnitude decomposition, in which the magnitude sets the update gain, i.e., how strongly an observation is written into the state, and the direction encodes the geometric intent, i.e., where the update drives the state. This decomposition provides a unified view of CUT3R and its variants, revealing that existing training-free extensions perform magnitude-only control: they can attenuate an unreliable update but cannot correct its direction. We propose HIST3R, a training-free framework built on CUT3R that controls both components using history. HIST3R rectifies the update direction using locally consistent historical states, and modulates the update magnitude according to the visual discrepancy between the current observation and its history, suppressing redundant updates while preserving complementary evidence. Across camera pose estimation, 3D reconstruction, and video depth estimation, HIST3R consistently improves long-horizon performance while retaining the memory footprint and inference speed of CUT3R. With 1000 input frames, it reduces ATE by 23.87% on ScanNet and 33.65% on TUM-Dynamics relative to the strongest competing method; with 500 frames, it improves median reconstruction accuracy over the strongest CUT3R-based variant by 56.52% on 7-Scenes and 33.96% on NRGBD.

title: Robust Domain-Mixture Scheduling for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) merges the capabilities of multiple domain-expert teachers, such as mathematical reasoning, code generation, and instruction following, into a single compact student. Since all domains share a limited training budget, how to allocate it across domains directly determines the quality of distillation. Existing methods allocate the budget by each domain's learning progress, but offer no guarantee for lagging domains. We therefore introduce distributionally robust optimization (DRO) into MOPD to prioritize the worst-performing domain. However, the per-domain training signals are estimated from a few rollouts and are inherently noisy, so directly applying DRO mistakes noise for the worst case, lets occasional spikes hijack the budget, and protects inherently hard domains rather than truly regressing ones. To address these issues, we propose RDS-MOPD, which keeps the DRO objective and redesigns its three parts: it shifts the allocation only when differences clearly exceed the noise, bounds the influence of any single anomaly, and defines the worst case as the regression from each domain's own best level, all with theoretical guarantees. Experiments show that RDS-MOPD outperforms recent competing methods and ranks first on most mathematical reasoning, code generation, and instruction-following benchmarks.

title: Enhancing Multi-Step Chemical Mechanism Prediction with Graph-Guided Preference Data
abstract: Predicting multi-step chemical reaction mechanisms requires identifying plausible intermediates and correctly ordering the elementary reaction steps. Existing computational methods focus on single-step elementary reaction prediction, limiting their ability to generalize to unseen reaction spaces. We introduce a graph-guided framework for multi-step chemical mechanism prediction that leverages a chemical mechanism knowledge graph (ChemMechKG) to guide large language models (LLMs). To improve pathway prediction, we develop a graph-aligned reaction mechanism predictor (GRMP) that uses graph neural networks to generate synthetic candidate pathways for pathway optimization. During inference, we design a relation retrieval (RR) module to extract relevant graph evidence from the KG for pathway refinement. Experiments show that GRMP achieves the highest pathway accuracy among all compared methods on ChemMechQA and oMe-Gold, reaching 48.1% and 57.9%, respectively. On a fixed sample of 110 out-of-distribution reactions from ChemMechQA-Hard, GRMP achieves 36.4% top-1 pathway accuracy. LLM-as-Judge and human assessment further demonstrate its ability to generalize to unseen reactions.

title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
abstract: Large language models and the multi-agent systems built around them could accelerate materials discovery by connecting scientific knowledge with experimental decisions. Existing benchmarks establish capabilities in domain knowledge, multimodal interpretation and scientific tool use. As language models increasingly support materials research workflows, their ability to distinguish closely related material states and reason accurately with quantitative evidence remains insufficiently evaluated. These abilities are essential for comparing material responses, assessing mechanisms and maintaining reliable judgements as experimental evidence accumulates. We introduce MatScope to evaluate three connected capabilities. M1 tests unaided, condition-specific reasoning through 200 tasks spanning ten research functions, using aluminium and high-entropy alloys as representative material systems. M2 tests agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions. MatEvoBench-20 tests initial forecasts across scientific dependency chains and revisions of still-hidden responses as observations accumulate. Across eleven model deployments, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, given-input calculations and many physical explanations are handled well. Fine-grained response estimates, comparisons between similar states and quantitatively supported choices remain substantially weaker. Related literature improves selected estimates, while condition and baseline mismatches limit transfer. Progressive observations calibrate some downstream responses and destabilize earlier accurate predictions. MatScope establishes measurable targets for developing reliable scientific reasoning in future self-evolving materials laboratories and materials-aware world models.

title: A Poisson-bracket operator for Hamiltonian separability: intrinsic geometry and exact defects
abstract: Additive separation of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation depends on the Hamiltonian and on the canonical variables, and this paper introduces a five-input Poisson-bracket operator whose values on canonical pairs reproduce the Levi-Civita separability expressions. On a symplectic product structure its off-diagonal values are intrinsic, since they equal a symplectic pairing of the sector Hamiltonian fields and measure the Frobenius obstruction of a Lagrangian distribution, and their vanishing yields a local separation theorem. Because the operator is cubic in the Hamiltonian, its perturbation expansion is exact and defines a linearised separability operator and a defect functional. For Hamiltonians with a cyclic angle, the linearised operator divided by the squared rotor frequency is an angle derivative of the Melnikov integrand, so that the defect integrated along a homoclinic orbit decides the first-order splitting of the separatrix. Closed-form defects are obtained for the polar-nodal normal forms of satellite theory and, through a covariance of the operator on level sets, for Kerr geodesics. Used for coordinate selection, the defect singles out the separating focal distance of the Euler two-centre problem as its unique nondegenerate minimum, and for axisymmetric potentials it shows that the prescriptions of Sanders and Vasiliev are two weightings of the same Stäckel residual. The residual selector and Binney's shell-orbit fit improve both actions over the median prescription for 48 and 50 of 50 orbits in a flattened logarithmic potential, whereas the operator selector lowers the 90th-percentile action spread of 50 orbits in a Miyamoto-Nagai potential from 2.90% to 0.91%.

title: Speculative Self-Distillation enables Efficient Knowledge Internalization
abstract: Many real-world applications require language models to internalize knowledge that was absent from pretraining, to incorporate continually updated facts, or to learn new domain skills. Self-distillation has emerged as a natural approach for this task. A model conditioned on the source material acts as the teacher, and an unconditioned student is trained to reproduce the teacher's behavior closed-book. We propose Speculative Self-Distillation (SSD), an efficient per-token mixed-policy method for self-distillation. The student generates each rollout by default, while the teacher intervenes only at positions where its next-token distribution substantially diverges from the student's. Unlike off-policy distillation with teacher-generated prefixes, this design keeps training rollouts close to the student's test-time behavior, while avoiding the low-signal states that fully on-policy rollouts drift into. In effect, SSD lets the teacher steer the rollout exactly where the privileged context changes the prediction. On three closed-book QA benchmarks measuring fact recall, knowledge updates, and skill acquisition, SSD nearly matches on-policy distillation while using 38-69% fewer supervised tokens and consistently outperforms off-policy distillation on the held-out test set. On a forgetting stress test, SSD retains the most general capability while also achieving the best in-domain accuracy and using less supervision than the on-policy baseline. Overall, SSD establishes a new accuracy-efficiency-forgetting Pareto frontier for self-distillation.

title: Grasp-Taxonomy Conditioning as a Mode Switch for Dexterous Grasping of Climbing Holds
abstract: Dexterous grasping in robotics relies on distinct hand configurations depending on object geometry. We introduce BetaGrasp, a 3D diffusion policy that conditions a DP3-style point-cloud policy on a four-class grasp label (crimp, sloper, pinch, and jug), running on a Franka arm with a 16-DoF LEAP hand. We also introduce a climbing-hold benchmark: a spring testbed whose ratchet gives a slip-force reading in newtons. In our analysis the policy's point-cloud encoder did not separate the four holds, so the scan alone gave it little to choose a grasp from. Without the label (a DP3-style baseline), simulated rollouts from the robot's reset pose all end in a jug grasp, whatever the hold (25% correct grasp type, versus 94% for BetaGrasp). The label works as a switch for which grasp the policy performs. On 80 paired hardware trials, BetaGrasp raises average slip force from 9.6 N to 14.3 N, and grasps slipping fully off the hold drop from 44% of trials to 10%.

title: Extending the reach of real-space real-time TDDFT: new developments in the Octopus code
abstract: Octopus is an open-source package implementing time-dependent density functional theory in a real-space, real-time formulation. Here we report on the developments since our previous contribution to the Special Topic Issue on Electronic Structure Software [J. Chem. Phys. 152, 124119 (2020)]. New exchange-correlation functionals extend the range of systems that can be treated, while advances in relativistic and all-electron methods open the door to core-electron spectroscopy. New capabilities for lattice dynamics - stress-tensor calculation, geometry optimization, support for machine-learned force fields, and phonon calculations - enable a fully ab initio description of light-induced lattice dynamics in real time. We also present developments that move beyond the dipole approximation, capturing light-matter interaction more faithfully. Improved methods for exciton dynamics complement a set of algorithmic advances - new propagation schemes, imaginary-time evolution, and a refactored grid handling more than a billion points - that together substantially improve performance and scalability. Combined with technical improvements such as AMD GPU support and a modernized build system, these developments consolidate Octopus as a versatile, high-performance platform for exploring electronic excitations, light-matter interaction, and nonequilibrium dynamics in molecules, nanostructures, and extended systems.

title: Feeling Easier, Working Harder: Cognitive Load in AI-Assisted Code Comprehension
abstract: Software developers spend significant time reading and understanding code, increasingly supplemented by generative AI. While these tools aim to reduce the difficulty of reading code, interacting with them introduces a dual-task environment that may impose extraneous cognitive load that is challenging to capture. This study investigates how access to generative AI affects developers' real-time cognitive workload, code comprehension performance, and self-perceived code comprehension strategies. We conducted a 3x2 within-subjects study with 20 novice CS students reviewing Java code snippets of varying lengths with or without AI assistance, followed by an AI-unassisted comprehension quiz. Cognitive workload was continuously captured using a Detection-Response Task (tDRT) during both reading and quiz phases, and compared to post-quiz NASA-TLX and SEQ scores. AI assistance significantly increased objective cognitive workload, raising tDRT reaction times by 11.2%, yet participants' perceived workload remained unchanged. Code comprehension scores were high under both conditions, with no evidence that AI assistance improved comprehension at the difficulty levels evaluated; a ceiling effect limited power to detect benefits on harder tasks. Qualitatively, participants reported trusting the AI conditionally -verifying its output against their own reading for more complex snippets, but directly trusting it for simpler code- and, while many felt their reading process was unchanged, a notable subset shifted toward skimming or reading the AI's explanations in place of the code itself. These findings reveal that developers do not accurately perceive the cognitive resources they expend when managing AI tools. This study provides evidence of added cognitive effort associated with using generative AI, pointing towards a need to account for this dual-task penalty in software engineering tools and education.

title: A generalized transition framework for identifying reduction domains in non-binary constituency parsing
abstract: Direct non-binary constituency parsing must identify an ordered sequence of children at each phrase-level reduction. We extend our earlier delimiter-guided bottom-up construction to a common calculus for top-down, in-order, and bottom-up parsing. At reduction, the rightmost delimiter marks the left boundary, the nonterminal marker supplies the mother label, and the completed items in the delimited segment determine the children and arity. We use a stack invariant to prove soundness and completeness and derive the exact length of the static oracle's action sequence. A projection-and-lifting theorem shows that each delimiter-guided system and its canonical counterpart generate the same set of trees under both the structural and grammar-licensed transition relations. In controlled experiments on PTB and CTB, the delimiter-guided parsers achieve similar labeled accuracy to their canonical counterparts across all traversal orders. For bottom-up parsing, delimiter guidance reduces the number of action classes and increases the number of supervised decisions per tree.

title: Near-Field Channel Estimation via Deep Unfolding for Extremely Large-Scale Antenna Arrays
abstract: The Extremely Large-scale Antenna Array (ELAA) has been envisioned as a promising candidate to meet the ambitious demands of 6G. However, this evolution also brings about two primary limitations: high computational complexity caused by large-scale arrays and inherent operation in the near-field region. To address these issues, this work exploits the sparsity of near-field channels in the polar domain and formulates channel estimation as a compressed sensing (CS) problem, thereby enabling estimation with reduced pilot overhead. In particular, we propose a guideline to design a sparsifying codebook for the near-field channel, which is strictly based on a target coherence value. Building on this, we develop a deep unfolding architecture, derived from the iterative solver ISTA, with a hybrid loss, namely Hybrid LISTA. Numerical results demonstrate that our proposed codebook, with comparable complexity, still exhibits improved estimation performance and greater coverage in the near-field region. Moreover, our unfolded model with the hybrid loss consistently delivers better recovery performance over existing estimation schemes.

title: A Finite-Lag Markov Chain Model for Coarse-Graining Linear SDEs
abstract: In this paper, we analyze a finite-lag Markov chain approximation for coarse-grained linear stochastic differential equations. The chain uses the limiting conditional transition law of the resolved variables to advance on a prescribed time grid. Its stability and statistical properties are studied, with particular attention to the role of the lag time. The chain preserves the exact equilibrium distribution and matches the autocovariance at the chosen lag, while errors at subsequent times are quantified. For a slow-fast system, the analysis relates lag selection to scale separation and dynamical accuracy. A continuous embedding of the chain enables a unified comparison with some existing continuous-time Markovian effective models based on the temporal statistics they preserve. Numerical examples illustrate the theoretical results.

title: TIRAD: Text-guided Image Residual Learning for Generalist Anomaly Detection
abstract: Recent anomaly detection studies have shown that residual features, which model the discrepancy between normal and abnormal patterns, provide strong generalization to anomalies unseen during training. However, existing residual-based approaches mainly rely on visual discrepancies derived from image representations, while semantic discrepancies that can be explicitly expressed through language remain largely underexplored. To address this problem, we propose TIRAD, Text-guided Image Residual Learning for Generalist Anomaly Detection, a multimodal residual learning framework that defines the discrepancy between textual representations of normal and abnormal states as a Text Residual Feature and uses it to guide the Image Residual Feature. Specifically, a Text Fusion Module converts patch-level text residuals into a gate that modulates the image residual of each patch. The gate retains the visual discrepancies that the text residual identifies as defect-related and attenuates the others, leading to more discriminative anomaly representations. Extensive experiments on industrial benchmarks and industrial-to-medical transfer demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing image-centric residual learning methods.

title: FocusBranch: Combinatorial Branch-and-Bound for $\ell_0$ Neural Network Robustness Verification
abstract: Verifying the local robustness of neural networks under $\ell_0$ perturbations is inherently combinatorial, as it must reason over all sparse subsets of $ε$ perturbed pixels. This paper presents FocusBranch, a combinatorial branch-and-bound framework for $\ell_0$ robustness verification. The key insight is to make the $\ell_0$-ball decomposable and branchable using a node abstraction, which consists of a focus pixel set $\mathcal{S}$ and a level $l$, permitting at most $ε-l$ pixels outside $\mathcal{S}$. This abstraction unifies two branching mechanisms: concrete nodes branch through upper shadows to fix additional perturbed locations, while super nodes branch through covering designs to cover many perturbation cases with fewer child nodes. FocusBranch proves node safety by concretizing linear relaxations over node-constrained $\ell_0$-balls and recursively branches on unknown nodes. Rather than relying on a fixed verification plan, it samples nodes across levels to estimate safe rates and costs, then selects a starting level and branching strategy predicted to minimize verification time. Experiments on fully connected and convolutional classifiers for MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 show that FocusBranch verifies $\ell_0$ robustness effectively across architectures and outperforms state-of-the-art verifiers. The code is available at: https://github.com/simpl-group/FocusBranch.

title: Single Image Super-Resolution via Semantic Prompt and Cross-Modal Training on Content Area
abstract: Enhancing image quality through super-resolution is crucial in image and video processing. While contemporary deep learning models, such as CNNs and Transformers, excel in pixel-level enhancements, they often overlook the rich semantic context within images. To address this, we introduce a novel approach that synergizes pixel intensity with semantic information for superior detail recovery. Our method involves extracting semantic data, including textual descriptors and spatial positioning, and encoding this information. We also present a Cross-Modal Feature Fusion module for generating semantic feature maps via multimodal training, and a Prompt Traction Head to augment the backbone network with semantic insights, thereby refining image details. Our empirical results across various datasets validate the superiority of our approach.

title: MambaPD: Bidirectional Selective State Space Model for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Resting-State EEG
abstract: Typical diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) occurs only after significant dopaminergic loss, while resting-state EEG abnormalities like alpha slowing and reduced coherence occur earlier. While many published EEG-based PD detectors claim accuracy greater than 95%, many use epoch-level splits which leak subject identity. I introduce MambaPD, a bidirectional selective state space model for resting-state EEG-based PD detection, blending the channel mixing, patch tokenization and bidirectional Mamba encoder. It is compared with four baselines (TCN, BiLSTM with attention, EEGNet and a patch Transformer) in two public datasets (UNM, SanDiego) using subject-independent 5-fold cross-validation (checkpoints were selected on the held-out fold, so absolute estimates are optimistic). On UNM the accuracy is between 0.67 and 0.71, and MambaPD (0.714) is not statistically distinguishable from the Transformer (0.715), and TCN (0.708), with the highest sensitivity (0.82), while the lowest specificity (0.52). For the smaller SanDiego cohort, accuracy is in the range of 0.60 to 0.70, with the highest scores (0.703) from TCN and the lowest (0.601) from EEGNet, while MambaPD scores 0.631, with the lowest specificity (0.46) among the five models. The differences among the models on UNM are minor compared to the differences among folds. I report the whole pipeline, per-fold results, and the shortcomings of the protocol.

title: An open source Python code for three-dimensional topology optimization in single precision on a consumer GPU
abstract: Three-dimensional topology optimization solves linear systems with millions of unknowns at every design iteration. Consumer graphics cards run far faster in single than in double precision, and open codes for them mostly address minimum compliance. This educational article presents TOF3D, an open source Python code for density-based topology optimization in single precision on one consumer GPU. It solves four classes of problems: stress constrained minimum compliance, robust minimum compliance against manufacturing errors, compliant mechanisms and bone-like porous infill. The stiffness operator is applied without assembly, and the conjugate gradient method is preconditioned by geometric multigrid. Rounding the element matrix to single precision gave rigid body motions a spurious energy and changed compliances by up to 5.4%. Forming the element products from differences of nodal displacements reduced this error to $1.3\times 10^{-5}$ at no cost in time. Adjoint sensitivities agreed with finite differences to within $1.7\times 10^{-6}$, and the solutions agreed with Ansys Mechanical APDL to within $4.1\times 10^{-10}$ with the same element. On an RTX 3060 with 12 GB, one design iteration of a cantilever took 0.46 s with 0.5 million elements and 15 s with 33.5 million. On the same card and problem, an open GPU code that applies its operator in double precision took 3.7 and 21 s with 0.5 and 4.2 million elements and ran out of memory on larger meshes. Eight cases fixed in a protocol before the runs took 9 to 35 minutes each with 4.2 to 5.2 million elements.

title: Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
abstract: We present SPOD-GPR, a non-intrusive, parametric, spatio-temporal reduced-order model (ROM) that combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), Spectral POD (SPOD), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). A parametric POD first projects the high-dimensional state onto a low-dimensional subspace. The reduced trajectories are then divided into windowed sections, transformed into the frequency domain, and truncated to the most energetic frequencies. SPOD is then performed independently at each retained frequency, yielding temporally coherent modes and coefficients. The parametric dependence of the POD and SPOD bases is modelled by GPR on a local chart of the Grassmann manifold after Procrustes alignment. The SPOD modal coefficients are learned both as explicit functions of the parameters and through a parameter-conditioned autoregressive model that allows for temporal extrapolation beyond the training window. Gaussian processes are sampled jointly and pathwise via Matheron conditioning, ensuring that each predictive realization carries uncertainty quantification consistent with the posterior distribution. The method is tested on four parametric examples where the parameter values and the prediction horizon lie outside the training data: the two-dimensional anisotropic Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation in a time-periodic and a travelling-wave regime, each parametrised by one of its two coefficients; flow past a cylinder parametrised by the Reynolds number; and flow past an elliptic obstacle parametrised by its semi-axes. In all cases, SPOD-GPR reduces the normalised mean absolute error compared to a POD-GPR baseline, and improves the calibration of the predictive uncertainty, especially in the fluid flow cases, where POD-GPR is severely overconfident. This opens the way to spectral, uncertainty-aware reduced-order models for many-query and real-time applications, such as digital twins.

title: Quasipositive and almost positive sectional curvature on finite quotients of Wallach spaces
abstract: We construct nonnegatively curved metrics on the cyclic and full permutation quotients of the Wallach flag manifolds in dimensions $6$, $12$, and $24$. The metrics are quasipositively curved in all three dimensions and almost positively curved in dimensions $12$ and $24$. The cyclic quotients are orientable with fundamental group $C_3$, and their further full permutation quotients have fundamental group $S_3$; none admits any metric of everywhere positive sectional curvature. For the almost-positive metrics we describe every zero-curvature plane and prove that the zero-point loci have Hausdorff dimensions exactly $11$ and $23$, respectively. A one-step deformation has, in each dimension, an explicit zero locus with nonempty interior. Further nested deformations reduce it to a measure-zero set while leaving a common codimension-one stratum. The argument combines normal forms for horizontal commuting planes with quaternionic rank conditions and a dimension estimate for commuting compressions of skew-symmetric operators. We also determine the possible degrees of arbitrary free finite quotients of the three flag covers and derive order bounds for fundamental groups when the Euler characteristic is nonzero. We have used ChatGPT-6-astra for mathematical exploration and verified and rewritten all the results.

title: Spectral conditions for the existence of $\{K_2,\{C_k\}\}$-factor in $t$-tough graphs
abstract: For $t>0$, a graph $G$ is called $t$-tough if $|S|\geq t\,c(G-S)$ for every $S\subseteq V(G)$ with $c(G-S)\geq2$, where $c(G-S)$ denotes the number of components of $G-S$. Toughness is closely related to the existence of Hamiltonian cycles and factors in graphs. Chvátal [Discrete Math. 5 (1973) 215--228] conjectured that there exists a constant $t_0>0$ such that every $t_0$-tough graph of order at least three is Hamiltonian. Bauer, Broersma and Veldman [Discrete Appl. Math. 99 (2000) 317--321] constructed $(9/4-\varepsilon)$-tough graphs without a Hamiltonian path for arbitrarily small $\varepsilon>0$. For the weaker requirement of a $2$-factor, Enomoto et al. [J. Graph Theory 9 (1985) 87--95] proved that every $2$-tough graph of order at least three has a $2$-factor and that the toughness threshold $2$ is best possible. A graph $G$ is said to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor if and only if $G$ contains a spanning subgraph consisting of components that are either cycles or single edges. A $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor can be viewed as a combination of a $1$-factor and a $2$-factor, motivating the study of such factors in tough graphs. In this paper, we establish sharp sufficient conditions in terms of the adjacency spectral radius, the distance spectral radius, and the distance signless Laplacian spectral radius for a $t$-tough graph to have a $\{K_2,\{C_k:k\geq3\}\}$-factor.

title: Scale-Invariant Empirical-Bayes Laplace Approximation for ReLU Networks
abstract: ReLU networks are well-known to have continuous scale symmetries; infinitely many reparameterized weight vectors that represent the same function. Dinh et al. (2017) have shown that, by reparameterizing, the geometry of the loss landscape (e.g., curvature) of these networks can be changed arbitrarily without affecting the underlying function. Thus, any quantity that depends on the network's geometry should be defined with care. In this paper, we show that the Empirical Bayes (EB) Laplace's approximation is not well-defined for ReLU networks, mainly due to Hessian dependence in computing the marginal likelihood, which is not invariant under ReLU scale symmetries. Thus, we can get different prior precisions, posterior covariances, and predictive uncertainties for a network having identical predictions under ReLU scaling. We define family of prior precision fields indexed by $γ$ and introduce $γ$-canonicalization, which first converts the network to its canonical representation by balancing the ratio of incoming to outgoing weights, and then fits the Empirical Bayes (EB) Laplace to the canonical representation. This procedure is equivalent to transporting the isotropic Gaussian prior from the canonical representation to the original coordinates, by producing a ReLU-scale-compatible precision field. This makes the marginal likelihood invariant under ReLU scaling, while allowing $γ$ to be selected by maximizing the marginal likelihood. The resulting EB Laplace approximation is well-defined on ReLU scale-equivalence classes and yields consistent prior precision selection and predictive uncertainties across functionally identical parameterizations.

title: Magnetotropic signatures of Fulde-Ferrell Pairing in a Pauli-limited superconductor
abstract: Resonant torsion magnetometry measures the angular curvature of the free energy and is sensitive to magnetic anisotropy. We calculate its response for a clean Pauli-limited superconductor with single-plane-wave Fulde-Ferrell pairing. Field rotation drives a first-order transition from the uniform condensate into the finite-momentum phase and a continuous transition into the normal state. The first-order line produces a sharp softening whose integrated weight is fixed by the magnetization jump, so the dip alone does not identify finite momentum. The distinguishing response is a broad softening inside the Fulde-Ferrell phase, caused by relaxation of the gap and pairing momentum, followed by a finite step at the upper critical field.

title: Aircraft speed and height from Doppler-shifted sound and flight-track data
abstract: The changing pitch of a passing aircraft is a familiar example of the Doppler effect. We use audio recordings of 40 aircraft passages to estimate the speed and height by two methods based on the Doppler effect. The endpoint method is an analytical model that uses the limiting frequencies at the start and end of each recording and the slope near the middle of the frequency-time curve. The second method fits the whole curve. Results from both methods are compared with independent flight-tracking data. The endpoint method consistently underestimates speed and height because the recorded frequencies have not approached their limiting values. The full curve fit agrees with the tracking data within about 3% in speed and 12% in height for steady passages, with poorer agreement when speed or height changes. Software developed with AI assistance made it practical to analyze this many passages. The comparison offers undergraduate students an example of testing model assumptions and identifying systematic errors in real measurements.

title: The Power of Migration on Identical Machines is Two
abstract: We study the power of migration in preemptive scheduling on identical parallel machines with time windows. If an instance admits a migratory schedule on $m$ machines, how many machines are needed to schedule it without migration? Kalyanasundaram and Pruhs (2001) showed that $6m-5$ machines suffice and gave a polynomial-time construction using $12m-5$ machines, whereas $2m-1$ machines may be necessary. We close this gap, which has been open for more than 25 years: $2m-1$ machines always suffice, and a corresponding non-migratory schedule can be computed in strongly polynomial time. Our proof has two main technical ingredients. First, we introduce supercanonical schedules and prove that the conflict graph of every such schedule on $m$ machines is $(2m-1)$-colorable. The key property is that whenever a job pauses, the jobs running alongside it just before and just after the pause separate the jobs processed entirely during the pause from the rest of the conflict graph. We use these separators and Kempe exchanges to compute a coloring in polynomial time. Second, we construct a supercanonical schedule with polynomially many processing blocks by shrinking job windows as far as possible while preserving feasibility and solving a min-cost flow problem.

title: Uniqueness of positive solutions of mixed Laplacian and fractional Laplacian in $\mathbb R$
abstract: We establish the uniqueness and nondegeneracy for positive finite-energy solutions of the following one-dimensional mixed Schrödinger equation \begin{equation} -Q'' + (-Δ)^s Q + Q = |Q|^p Q \quad \text{in } \mathbb R, \end{equation} where $0<s<1$ and $p>0$. For every $0<s<1, p>0$, we obtain the corresponding results for positive solutions whose linearized operators have Morse index equal to one. We extend the nodal analysis developed by Frank-Lenzmann-Silvestre to the mixed operator establishing the monotonicity of the quotient of a hypothetical nontrivial even kernel element by $-Q'$. We then combine this monotonicity with oscillation estimates to prove nondegeneracy, and uniqueness follows by continuation. Moreover, for every $1/2\le s<1,p>0$, both uniqueness and nondegeneracy hold for positive solutions. Our novelty is to use the properties of Green kernel of the mixed operator to derive the upper bound and lower bound on the maximum of each solution. This peak estimate allows us to prove uniqueness by direct comparison and to establish nondegeneracy.

title: Split-Ring Couplers for On-Skin Wi-Fi Communication via an SSPP Waveguide Textile
abstract: Textile spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) waveguides offer guided on-body links, but their body-facing ground conductors obstruct coupling from on-skin wireless nodes. This letter presents a split-ring coupling interface using local ground recesses at the textile terminations, without patterned garment-side launchers. The capacitively loaded rings are supported by polydimethylsiloxane carriers with a thickness of 2~mm. An image-current model and full-wave simulations examine the effect of backing-ground spacing and determine the recess geometry. For a 450~mm textile waveguide on a water-filled body phantom, the measured $S_{21}$ at 2.45 GHz was $-$18.8~dB, versus $-$60.9~dB without the textile. A 625-position scan showed a maximum 5.1 dB reduction relative to the nominal position within the measured joint $\pm$5~mm placement region. A separate two-node IEEE~802.11n test demonstrated a 65~Mb/s physical-layer (PHY) rate with zero packet errors among 300 frames at $-$20~dBm transmit power through the coupler link. These results establish high-rate, placement-tolerant on-skin Wi-Fi communication through an SSPP waveguide textile.

title: SAFE-Hair: Scalp-Anchored Fields for Exportable Single-View Hair Reconstruction
abstract: Single-view 3D hair reconstruction has progressed rapidly, but many methods optimize for visual plausibility rather than producing strand assets that can be directly used in grooming, editing, or simulation pipelines. We propose SAFE-Hair, a framework that reconstructs explicit strand grooms from a single portrait by decoding hair from persistent follicles in a canonical scalp-UV domain. Given a fitted template head, SAFE-Hair projects self-supervised image features onto the scalp, uses a conditional Rectified Flow model to generate latent scalp fields, and decodes occupancy, segment directions, length allocation, and total length at a fixed set of scalp follicles. This representation enforces scalp-rooted strand identities by construction and enables direct export with follicle IDs and guide-family metadata. We further introduce attachment, collision, and bending priors to improve geometric validity without per-subject test-time optimization. To evaluate both reconstruction fidelity and asset usability, we introduce HairBench-3D, a benchmark built from public 3D hair assets with standardized alignment, rendering, resampling, and metrics for geometry, direction consistency, invisible-region completion, silhouette agreement, and collision. SAFE-Hair improves Chamfer distance from 3.74 mm to 3.28 mm, F-score from 77.9 to 81.7, invisible-region F-score from 66.1 to 69.8, and penetration ratio from 4.8% to 3.9% over the strongest baseline.

title: DPGS-SLAM: Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM for Dynamic Visual Sensing
abstract: This paper presents DPGS-SLAM (Diffusion-Prior and Provenance-Aware Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM) for dense mapping in environments containing dynamic objects. Dynamic observations can contaminate camera tracking and scene reconstruction in visual SLAM (simultaneous localization and mapping). Although 3DGS (3D Gaussian splatting) enables efficient dense mapping, existing 3DGS-SLAM systems may exhibit instability when dynamic objects violate their underlying static-scene assumption. Excluding dynamic observations can reduce their influence on tracking and mapping, but may leave occluded static backgrounds missing or weakly constrained. Our proposed DPGS-SLAM is a monocular RGB SLAM framework that supports provisional representations of insufficiently observed static backgrounds through asynchronous diffusion-based background completion and provenance-aware Gaussian mapping. Dynamic regions are identified through optical-flow-based motion discovery and temporally consistent mask propagation by SAM2 (segment anything model 2). For selected keyframes, a fine-tuned diffusion inpainting model generates plausible background appearance in occluded regions, while Metric3D v2 predicts metric depth from the completed images to initialize provisional Gaussian primitives. Provenance labels distinguish generated primitives from observation-supported primitives, excluding generated content from camera-pose estimation and observed-map optimization. When previously occluded backgrounds become visible, eligible generated primitives are removed, and observation-supported primitives are independently initialized from real RGB observations and predicted depth. Experimental results demonstrated competitive camera tracking, with average ATE RMSE values of 1.2 cm on TUM RGB-D and 2.7 cm on BONN RGB-D. On StaDy4D, DPGS-SLAM improved average PSNR by 4.60 dB over WildGS-SLAM using only monocular RGB input.

title: Adding minimal fresh subsets to $\aleph_ω$
abstract: Assuming the existence of a measurable cardinal, we produce generic extensions $V_1\subsetneq V_2$ of the universe with the same cardinals, cofinalities, and bounded subsets of $\aleph_ω$, such that $V_2$ is generated over $V_1$ by a cofinal $ω$-sequence in $\aleph_ω$, and $V_2$ is a minimal generic extension over $V_1$, i.e., every set of ordinals in $V_2\setminus V_1$ generates $V_2$ over $V_1$.

title: Leveraging Complementary Event Frame and Voxel Representations for RGB-Guided Multimodal Pre-training
abstract: In this paper, we propose CM3AE 2.0, a unified RGB Frame and Event-Voxel/-Frame pre-training framework. By jointly learning multimodal spatiotemporal representations and exploiting latent cross-modal dependencies through cross-modal generation, the framework enhances multimodal information interaction and collaborative modeling capabilities. Specifically, we first propose an Event-aware Spatiotemporal Masked Reconstruction (ESMR) strategy to learn unified multimodal spatiotemporal representations. It leverages event responses to guide masking toward dynamically salient regions. Through spatiotemporal masked reconstruction, it learns spatial structures and their temporal variations from continuous RGB-Event observations. In addition, it incorporates multimodal fusion reconstruction and cross-modal contrastive learning to facilitate the modeling of cross-modal complementary information and the learning of shared representations. Building upon this, we further propose a Hierarchical Cross-modal Generation (HCG) strategy to learn latent cross-modal dependencies through visual and language generation. At the visual level, Event-conditioned RGB generation is performed using a pre-trained diffusion model to capture visual associations between the two modalities. At the language level, video-level text description generation based on joint RGB-Event representations establishes connections between multimodal visual features and linguistic semantics, further enriching the learning of cross-modal dependencies. Extensive experiments on four diverse downstream tasks demonstrate that CM3AE 2.0 consistently improves performance, validating the effectiveness and generalization capability of the proposed pre-training framework.

title: SMO: Compiling Natural Language Skills into Graphs of Reusable State-Move-Outcome Bricks
abstract: Large language model agents increasingly rely on reusable natural-language skills, yet growing skill collections remain accumulations of isolated text artifacts that are difficult to compare, deduplicate, and compose. We argue that the reusable content of a skill lies not in its surface wording but in its procedural transitions: which operation to execute under a given state and which observable outcome to produce. Based on this observation, we propose State-Move-Outcome (SMO), a compilation-like framework that decomposes raw skills into reusable procedural bricks and organizes admitted bricks as an externalized symbolic structure. When compiling a skill, SMO first retrieves and composes existing bricks, dynamically connects them through Outcome-to-State conditions, and creates a candidate brick only for an uncovered procedure; the candidate becomes reusable only after validation and admission. Experiments on SkillsBench v1.1 demonstrate that SMO represents 232 rawSkills from 87 underlying tasks with 95 shared bricks, reducing the corresponding skill representations from 366,472 to 149,154 tokens--a $\mathbf{59.3}\times$ reduction and $\mathbf{2.46}\times$ compression. Across 232 skill-conditioned evaluation instances, SMO raises the average task score from $\mathbf{0.6379}$ to $\mathbf{0.7478}$ and increases 5/5 Pass instances from $\mathbf{138}$ to $\mathbf{164}$, while matching or outperforming rawSkill on $\mathbf{208}$ of $\mathbf{232}$ instances. It also reduces average runtime token consumption by $\mathbf{38.38\%}$. These results show that compiling natural-language skills into shared procedural units can jointly improve skill reuse, representation efficiency, and downstream execution.

title: Four-Step Text-Bearing Image Generation via Distillation with Local Response Regularization and Teacher-Guided Training
abstract: Generating text-bearing images requires coherent scenes and accurate characters. Large text-to-image models improve both capabilities through repeated denoising, at substantial sampling cost. Few-step distillation reduces this cost but requires the student to organize scenes and refine glyphs within a short trajectory. We present a four-step distillation framework combining local response regularization with teacher-guided text training. Built on distribution matching, the framework distills the GLM-Image DiT while retaining its autoregressive visual prior, glyph encoder, and VAE. A path-length penalty promotes consistent local responses of the conditional denoising field. Progressive training combines synthetic strings with teacher-generated imagery to preserve character accuracy and scene-integrated typography. The student achieves GenEval Overall 0.84 and CVTG-2K word accuracy 0.5045, compared with 0.81 and 0.1690 for four-step TDM. A coefficient study favors $10^{-5}$, and Qwen-Image experiments show additional gains from response regularization and text supervision. Single-image inference takes 1.742 s, compared with 5.818 s for the teacher, yielding a $3.34\times$ speedup at the same 40 GB GPU memory requirement.

title: $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded norms for de Rham-Witt forms
abstract: We make two case studies of $\mathrm{RO}(G)$-graded homotopy in connection with $p$-adic cohomology. First, we identify the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf T)$-graded $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$ of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings as multi-Rees algebras for the Nygaard and $ϕ^\bullet(I)$-adic filtrations. We additionally compute $E^{h\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ and $E^{t\mathbf T}_\bigstar$ when $E$ is a general even $\mathbf E_\infty$-ring with $\mathbf T$-action, and compute $(\mathrm{TR}^n)^{h\mathbf T/C_{p^n}}_\bigstar$ in terms of iterated Nygaard filtrations. Next, we compute the $\mathrm{RO}(\mathbf Z_p)^\land$-graded $\mathrm{TR}$ of smooth algebras over a perfectoid base, providing a pushout of the works of Hesselholt and Angeltveit-Gerhardt along the base case $\mathbf F_p$. Using this, we extend Angeltveit's Norm map of Witt vectors to the de Rham-Witt complex, which participates in a "Witt coordinates" decomposition of the $p$-primary Adams operations.

title: Leveraging High-Activity Post-Therapeutic I-131 Scans for Deep Learning Reconstruction of Extremely Sparse Planar Images in Differentiated Thyroid Cancer
abstract: Background: Diagnostic I-131 whole-body planar imaging in differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) is count-limited by low administered activity, and quality worsens under rapid acquisition. Models trained on such data struggle because their targets lack photon statistics. Purpose: To test whether high-quality post-therapeutic (PT) I-131 scans can serve as superior training references for enhancing sparse diagnostic planar images, using transfer learning and input-image addition. Methods: In this single-center prospective study, 111 patients were enrolled in PT training (n = 19), diagnostic follow-up (FU) training (n = 58), and FU paired test (n = 34) cohorts. Five Restormer-based models were trained: FU_DLx2 on FU labels; PT_DLx2 transfer-learned on PT data; PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ with input-image addition; PT_DLx6 as a PT-only reference. Test-time processing used two-step denormalization and Poisson re-scaling to preserve noise statistics. Quality was assessed by PSNR, SSIM, and a blinded dual-reader evaluation of all 34 test-cohort patients. Results: PT_DLx2 achieved the highest PSNR (34.4 +/- 3.6 dB) and SSIM (0.81 +/- 0.07). PT_DLx1+ and PT_DLx2+ were comparable (33.8 and 33.3 dB; SSIM 0.80). FU_DLx2 ranked below the unprocessed fast scan (30.3 vs. 32.0 dB; 0.76 vs. 0.79). Subjectively, PT_DLx2+ scored highest in image quality (4.54 +/- 0.60) and diagnostic confidence (4.54 +/- 0.60), surpassing the reference standard (4.19 +/- 0.83 and 4.31 +/- 0.81; P = 0.005 and P = 0.008). FU_DLx2 and PT_DLx6 scored lowest. Conclusion: Count-rich PT scans provide effective training priors for reconstructing extremely sparse images. Input-image addition and cross-domain transfer learning from PT data outperformed direct training on count-limited diagnostic data, supporting 2x scan acceleration with quality matching or exceeding the unaccelerated standard scan for selected PT-derived configurations.

title: Variational principles for dissipative continua: transport theorems, inertia, and the minimum-maximum duality
abstract: Variational principles for dissipative processes come in two families: minimum principles at nonequilibrium stationary states (Helmholtz, Kirchhoff, Prigogine) and maximum principles for relaxation in continuum mechanics (Ziegler, Hackl, Fischer). We contribute to the understanding of the thermodynamic extremal principle (TEP) by investigating its extremal properties, and uncover the connection between the two families, whose distinction was recently made precise for diffusion: the extremal character is decided by the regime, which is either relaxation at frozen state, as in a closed system (maximum dissipation), or a driven stationary state in an open system (minimum dissipation), while the underlying Rayleighian functional is convex and minimized in both cases. We further examine the Reynolds transport theorem, a useful tool for fixing the energy rates of continua, and the role of inertia, recently argued to lie beyond the reach of Rayleighian principles. With inertia the driving force must be held fixed during the variation, which is less elegant than in the inertialess case, where it is a state function. Writing the energy rate as rates times driving forces still yields the correct equations, and an extremal statement survives whenever the frozen force does not depend on the varied rate. This holds directly for unsteady Stokes flow, and for Navier-Stokes flow after a change to material coordinates, in which the particle acceleration is the second time derivative of the state and the convective term, nonvariational in the Eulerian description, does not appear. The framework is tested on the Navier-Stokes family (Stokes, unsteady Stokes, and Navier-Stokes flow, in order of increasing complexity) and on dissipative Lagrangian mechanics.

title: Could globular clusters in the vicinity of the galactic centre have contributed stars to the nuclear star cluster in the past?
abstract: The results of direct N-body simulations of three Milky Way bulge globular clusters - Terzan 2, Terzan 4, and Terzan 5 - evolving in a time-varying galactic potential derived from the IllustrisTNG-100 cosmological database over 8 Gyr are presented. Incorporating full stellar evolution and compact remnant formation, we quantify the probability and efficiency of stellar accretion onto the Galactic nuclear star cluster (NSC) during close pericentre passages of these three clusters. To parametrize the effect of dynamical friction in the dense central environment, we introduce a velocity reduction factor (Vred) ranging from 1.00 to 0.10. It was found that all three clusters contribute stars to the NSC even in the absence of velocity reduction, with a combined bound stellar count of 730 stars and a total accreted mass of 278 Msol at Vred = 1.00, growing to 5420 stars and 1175 Msol at Vred = 0.10. Terzan 4 is the dominant contributor across all velocity reduction factors, reflecting its more frequent and closer pericentre passages near the Galactic centre. The mass distribution of accreted stars reveals a bimodal structure: a low-mass component below 1 Msol whose capture is independent of Vred, and a prominent high-mass tail extending to 20 Msol corresponding to neutron stars and black holes, which grows with decreasing Vred. Notably, Terzan 4 is the only cluster for which white dwarfs are also captured by the NSC at every Vred value. Our results suggest that the Terzan family represents a more significant source of compact remnants for the Galactic NSC than previously studied clusters, while confirming that tidal stripping of surviving globular clusters alone cannot account for the total NSC mass.

title: Dust in cold and warm dark matter in a suite of zoom-in simulations of Milky Way analogues
abstract: We use a suite of hydrodynamical zoom-in simulations of Milky Way analogues to investigate how previously identified trends in dust properties of galaxies can be utilised to infer the underlying dark matter model. We use a sample of 24 comparison simulations comparing a cold dark matter (CDM) and 3.5 keV warm dark matter (WDM) particle, primarily using a dust-to-metals (DTM) ratio to post-process the dust in the simulation, with alternative methods explored. We find a preference for higher dust masses in CDM over WDM, with a median increase of 6.6 per cent in the CDM sample at redshift $z=0$, and with a peak median difference of 25 per cent at $z\approx0.25$. Both CDM and WDM samples are highly concentrated, with approximately 90 per cent of the dust located in the inner region of the halo, though slightly higher in CDM. Contrary to previous work, we find that the Gini coefficient does not consistently show a difference in comparisons of dark matter models, with differences primarily driven by high sensitivity to the unique structure of individual haloes. Finally, we conduct an analysis of some common dust scaling relations, finding that the differences between the two samples in the dust-to-stellar mass and dust-to-SFR functions do not constitute a statistically significant difference at $z=0$ with any dust production mechanism. However, at redshifts where the difference in dust mass is greatest, the alternative dust production methods show larger separations between CDM and WDM samples in total mass and scaling relations.

title: Evaluating AI Agents for Industrial-Level Chip Floorplanning: A Framework and Empirical Study
abstract: Floorplanning is an early step in turning a logical circuit into a physical chip: it positions large circuit modules and constrains the space available for subsequent logic placement and wiring. These decisions affect congestion and timing, but their physical consequences emerge through downstream implementation. For AI agents, the task requires translating engineering constraints into spatial decisions whose quality cannot be judged by successful tool execution alone. We present an evaluation framework that connects submitted layouts to a prescribed downstream implementation flow, checks geometric validity, measures physical quality, and reports resource use. On one industrial design whose 99 macros occupy approximately 71\% of a fixed L-shaped layout region, we compare our specialized system Nova-SI with general-purpose engineering agents and agents restricted to file access, obtaining complete physical measurements for 39 layout outputs. Under our 0--100 composite quality score, Nova-SI achieves a mean of 57.97 without online feedback from the prescribed power-grid and placement evaluation, compared with 31.17 for the strongest measured general-purpose configuration, GPT-6 Astra. The difference is supported by raw congestion and timing measurements and persists across scoring-sensitivity checks. Layout-level analysis further shows that similar global utilization can conceal substantially different local congestion. Together, the protocol and case study assess agents through the physical consequences of their delivered layouts and provide evidence about system performance on this industrial instance.

title: Parameterized equivalence checking of quantum circuit generators via weighted automata
abstract: A generator builds a quantum circuit from the number of qubits and a bit string. We check a generator against a reference for all parameter values under six equivalence relations. For ladder programs, we prove that above a computable threshold the circuit matrices form a uniform matrix product operator, a weighted automaton of dimension independent of the number of qubits. Equivalence reduces to the zeroness of a difference automaton, checked modulo primes. The answer is a counterexample or "equal", exact or with a computed error bound. Experimentally, the method found errors missed by fixed-size checks and produced no incorrect verdicts.

title: Deviations from Kerr: Critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters for general observer inclinations
abstract: We study critical curves and photon-ring critical parameters in stationary, axisymmetric spacetimes with separable null geodesics and Kerr angular structure. A Kerr-relative decomposition of the radial metric functions gives analytic first-order departures of these observables for observers at general inclination. The critical curve's signed normal displacement factorizes as $\tilde u_n=\tilde F_{\mathrm K}\mathscr C$, where $\tilde F_{\mathrm K}$ depends only on the Kerr reference geometry and $\mathscr C$ is an explicit combination of optical metric deviations. The demagnification exponent, time delay, and azimuthal advance are evaluated at a common position angle on the observer screen. Intrinsic relations among the exact observables express the optical information shared by the curve, time delay, and azimuthal advance, while demagnification additionally depends on radial instability. Applications to representative metrics illustrate how different radial deformations produce distinct departures from Kerr around the critical curve. Comparisons with exact finite-deformation profiles and independent numerical calculations verify the first-order predictions on regular, accessible exterior photon-shell branches.

title: Attention-Guided Sequence Feature Fusion and Mixed-Space Metric Learning for Cross-View Image Sequence Geo-Localization
abstract: Cross-view image sequence geo-localization aims to determine the geographic location of a sequence of ground images by matching it against geo-tagged satellite imagery. Although sequential observations provide complementary scene information, substantial overlap between adjacent images introduces feature redundancy, while conventional fusion strategies may weaken spatial relationships essential for cross-view matching. Therefore, we propose a cross-view image sequence geo-localization method via Attention-guided Sequence fusion and Metric Learning (ASML). Specifically, a Sequential Content Fusion (SCF) module models cross-image feature correlations to suppress redundant content and adaptively preserve geographically informative non-overlapping regions. Next, a Spatial Feature Aggregation (SFA) module is used to capture and aggregate the spatial and semantic information of local features, so as to maintain the spatial layout of the image sequence. Finally, a Geo-InfoNCE loss function is proposed, which comprehensively considers the feature distance and geographic distance for mixed-space metric learning, thus improving the ability of the model to distinguish hard negative samples. A new cross-view image sequence dataset CrossRoad-66K is established to provide more complex scenarios. Extensive experiments and visualizations on the SeqGeo and CrossRoad-66K datasets demonstrate that compared to state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, the proposed method ASML achieves an improvement of 3.37% and 2.10% at R@1, respectively.

title: Smooth asymptotically Self-similar blow up for the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$
abstract: We construct blow up solutions to the scalar Zakharov system in dimension $3$. More precisely, we construct the solutions $(ψ,n)$ defined for $t\in[0,T)$, blowing up at $t=T$ and taking the form \begin{align} ψ(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{T-t}P\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right)e^{i(T-t)^{-1/3}}, n(t,x) \sim\frac{1}{3(T-t)^{4/3}}N\left(\frac{|x|}{\sqrt{3}(T-t)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\right) \end{align} in the region $|x|\ll 1$. Here $(P,N)$ is the solution to a specified ODE system related to Zakharov system. The solutions we construct are smooth for $0\leq t<T$. Moreover, there exist $n_0,n_1\in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^3\backslash\{0\})$ with bounded support such that for any $r>0$, $(ψ,n,\partial_t n)$ converge to $(0,n_0,n_1)$ in $C^{\infty}(|x|>r)$. We correct the profile $(P,N)$ and obtain a sequence of approximate solutions that coincide in the region $|x|\gtrsim 1$ with higher and higher accuracy. Then we apply perturbative analysis to construct solutions with arbitrarily high finite regularity. The fixed point argument in this procedure actually yields that these solutions are the same for $t$ sufficiently close to $T$, which combined with the persistence of high regularity gives the existence of smooth asymptotically self-similar blow up solutions.

title: BECON: Belief-Conditioned Constrained Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning under Drifting Preferences and Budgets
abstract: Constrained preference-conditioned MORL typically assumes full task observability, treating preferences and safety budgets as stationary task signals. In real-world deployment, however, these signals are often unreliable proxies: intent may drift, safety tolerances may shift with context, and exposed descriptors may be noisy, delayed, or incomplete. We therefore formulate constrained preference-conditioned MORL as a partially observed task-specification problem, where the agent must navigate a fundamental conflict between unreliable external signals and latent interaction dynamics. We propose \textbf{BECON}, a belief-conditioned framework for constrained MORL with drifting preferences and budgets, which infers latent task context from recent histories to estimate preferences and safety budgets. These estimates are fused with the exposed task signal via uncertainty-dependent gates, enabling the policy to defer to observations under high epistemic uncertainty while correcting them when history is informative. The fused context jointly conditions preference optimization and context-adaptive constraint enforcement. Experiments on diverse multi-objective control tasks demonstrate that BECON consistently improves over state-of-the-art MORL baselines, achieving stronger robustness and constraint satisfaction under task drift.

title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
abstract: Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.

title: Equality in the direction bound over prime fields
abstract: Let $p$ be prime. We prove that a noncollinear set of $2m+1\le p$ points in $\AG(2,p)$ determines exactly $m+2$ directions if and only if, up to an affine transformation, it consists of the origin and a coset of a multiplicative subgroup of order $m$ on each coordinate axis. Thus equality is possible precisely when $m\mid p-1$. This extends the Lovász--Schrijver classification for $2m+1=p$.

title: One number per hour is not enough: directional carbon intensity of data-center ramps on the PJM fleet
abstract: A data-center campus can change its load by hundreds of megawatts within an hour, yet every carbon signal in use gives one value per hour for a load change, whatever its size or direction. We compute the directional carbon intensity, the emission caused or avoided per megawatt-hour of a finite upward or downward ramp, for every hour of 2025 on the PJM Interconnection's fossil fleet, and compare it with the locational marginal emission rate (LME) and the regional average. The LME misstates a 1 GW ramp by more than 10% in 60% to 83% of hours in eleven months. Upward and downward ramps differ in a quarter to three quarters of hours but agree on their monthly mean. Location-based reporting assigns 47% to 59% of a ramp's emission to other consumers. A campus should schedule on the signal for its ramp's size and direction and report the emission it causes.

title: AscendMOEA: An Ascend NPU-Accelerated Platform for Tensorized Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Multi-objective evolutionary optimization increasingly involves large populations, expensive problem evaluations, and diverse algorithmic structures. These workloads expose the limited parallelism of loop-based implementations, while rewrites for accelerator execution can alter selection order, tie handling, and population updates. AscendMOEA is presented as a scalable platform that executes multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) on Huawei Ascend neural processing units (NPUs) and conventional central processing units (CPUs). The platform represents the decision vectors, objectives, constraints, and auxiliary states as tensors and provides reusable interfaces for algorithms, problems, population operators, quality indicators, monitoring, and repeated experiments. Dense computations are executed in batches, such as dominance, distance, variation, and problem-evaluation calculations. Short recurrences with causal dependencies retain their prescribed order and consume precomputed tensor results, which preserves the behavior of the original algorithms. AscendMOEA contains 18 algorithms, 155 benchmark and application problems, 19 public operator interfaces, and 11 quality indicators. Experiments on eight Ascend NPUs and 192 physical CPU cores evaluate operator throughput, end-to-end runtime, memory consumption, numerical agreement, and implementation ablation. Tensorized operators obtain a median acceleration of 1.58 times on the NPU. At large population scales, complete algorithms achieve a median acceleration of 5.76 times while retaining the recorded quality indicators. Moreover, the results identify the workload scale and ordered computation that determine whether accelerator execution is beneficial. AscendMOEA is open-sourced at https://github.com/dqlme/AscendMOEA.

title: Exact Natarajan Dimension of Homogeneous Multiclass Linear Predictors
abstract: The Natarajan dimension is a fundamental measure of the capacity of multiclass hypothesis classes and plays an important role in analyzing their generalization ability. In this paper, by establishing lower and upper bounds, we show that the exact Natarajan dimension of homogeneous multiclass linear predictors with pairwise distinct class weights is \(n(k-1)-1\), where $n$ is the dimension of the feature space and $k$ is the number of classes, for \(n,k\ge3\), \(n,k\in\mathbb N\).

title: A Black-Box Reduction from Regret to Multi-Level Coverage
abstract: Online Conformal Prediction (OCP) sequentially constructs prediction sets whose average empirical coverage converges to a target level over time, for arbitrary, potentially adversarial datasets. In the multi-level setting, prediction sets are produced at $d$ coverage levels at once. Prior work argued for the use of online gradient descent with isotonic projections, which produces sets nested across levels, but with a $\sqrt{d}$ dependence in the per-level coverage convergence rate. Here, we both generalize and improve prior work. First, we show that isotonic projections can be used for the construction of multi-level online conformal prediction sets from \emph{any} online learning algorithm (not just gradient descent). Then, through a black-box reduction, we show that the linearized regret of the online algorithm itself automatically gives control over both per-level coverage and distributional consistency of multi-level predictions via Fenchel duality. Finally, by using the Weighted Interval Score, a standard scoring rule for assessing multi-level interval forecasts, we prove that these projections reduce both the size of the sets and their under-coverage. We study two instantiations of our theory, $p$-norm Online Mirror Descent and coordinate-wise Universal Portfolio methods, both improving the dependence on the number of levels to $\sqrt{\log d}$ for the multi-level OCP problem. Experiments on several datasets show favorable performance compared to baselines.

title: COMPASS: Composable Policy-Amortized Structured Search for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
abstract: Large language models offer a promising technique for translating natural-language optimization problems into solver code, but their reliability remains constrained by the quality of template retrieval. While recent structured methods improve over flat prompting through hierarchical taxonomy search, their traversal rules remain fixed or LLM-driven at inference time, leaving retrieval unable to improve from past successes and failures. This motivates treating template retrieval as a policy that can be learned from modeling experience, rather than as a static inference-time rule. We propose COMPASS, a policy-amortized framework for retrieving optimization templates in LLM-based solver modeling, which represents the template library as a directed acyclic graph and formulates retrieval as a sequential decision process over template nodes. A deep Q-network learns a reusable traversal policy from template-level judgments and execution feedback, reducing reliance on fixed heuristic traversal through feedback-driven graph navigation. To support extensible retrieval, COMPASS embeds problem descriptions and template nodes in a shared semantic space, allowing newly inserted templates to be scored from their text descriptions without redefining the action space. Experiments across multiple LLM backbones and optimization-modeling benchmarks demonstrate that COMPASS consistently improves over heuristic structured retrieval, with the largest gains on complex and mixed-category problems.

title: BARS: Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis via Flow Matching
abstract: We present BARS (Beat-Adaptive Rap Synthesis), a non-autoregressive rapping voice generation model based on Flow Matching, conditioned on a beat track (instrumental backing), lyrics, and a short reference voice for zero-shot timbre control. Unlike prior autoregressive rap synthesis, where rap pace and output duration are strictly determined by the beat, BARS enables independent control over the rap tempo, allowing flexible-length generation without explicit duration prediction or phoneme-level alignment. We encode lyrics using a pretrained ByT5 encoder with a lightweight Transformer adapter trained jointly with the model, without relying on speech-pretrained text encoders, enabling natural handling of non-standard orthography (e.g., slang, abbreviations) and numerals common in rap lyrics. To address alignment instabilities, such as token skipping or repetition, under strong beat conditioning, we propose Asymmetric Scaled RoPE for cross-attention, which introduces a positional structure to facilitate sequential lyric-audio alignment learning. Furthermore, the model supports partial re-generation via span masking, enabling lyric-level editing while preserving the surrounding vocal style. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves high lyric fidelity, natural rap flow that is rhythmically coherent with the beat, and robust tempo control across a wide range of rapping styles and speeds.

title: Translating KV Caches Between Hybrid-Attention Language Models: MLA Latents, Linear-Attention States and Sparse-Attention Indexers
